study_context.outcome: Alive and independent (Oxford Handicap Score 0-2) at 6 months
study_context.population: Acute ischemic stroke patients within 6 hours of symptom onset

Middle-aged patients (age >= 60 and < 70.hypothesis: Middle-aged patients (age >= 60 and < 70 years) derive a moderate benefit from IV alteplase because they retain sufficient physiological reserve with moderate vascular comorbidity.

In acute ischemic stroke patients treate.hypothesis: In acute ischemic stroke patients treated within 6 hours, those with weight >=90 kg will have a lower probability of being alive and independent (Oxford Handicap Score 0-2) at 6 months when randomized to IV alteplase compared with control.

subgroup_rule.description: Patients with weight greater than or equal to 90 kilograms

Acute ischemic stroke patients with admi.hypothesis: Acute ischemic stroke patients with admission glucose < 4.0 mmol/L are less likely to achieve independence (OHS 0-2) at 6 months after IV alteplase compared with patients with higher glucose.

subgroup_rule.description: Admission blood glucose less than 4.0 mmol/L (hypoglycemia)

Patients with moderate impaired consciou.hypothesis: Patients with moderate impaired consciousness (GCS 9–12) are more likely to be alive and independent at 6 months when treated with IV alteplase within 6 hours compared with patients outside this GCS range.

Among acute ischemic stroke patients tre.hypothesis: Among acute ischemic stroke patients treated within 6 hours, those with baseline NIHSS ≤ 7 will have a higher probability of being alive and independent (OHS 0–2) at 6 months when treated with IV alteplase compared with control.
